questions.prompt: You are modelling a checkout service that uses a pricing policy and a receipt sender. Their implementations may change independently. Which design is easiest to test and replace?
options: Put all behavior in one global object.
Make every service inherit from the receipt sender.
Inject pricing and receipt interfaces as collaborators (composition).
Duplicate all logic in every checkout method.
questions.answer_key: Inject pricing and receipt interfaces as collaborators (composition).
questions.explanation: Composition represents “has-a” relationships and makes collaborators replaceable for tests without forcing an inheritance relationship.

questions.prompt: A property should notify observers when its value changes. Which Kotlin standard delegate is most directly designed for this?
options: lazy
Delegates.observable
Delegates.notNull for every type
A custom setter that suppresses every update
questions.answer_key: Delegates.observable
questions.explanation: `Delegates.observable` invokes a callback after a property changes; `vetoable` is the related option for conditionally rejecting updates.

questions.prompt: A generic repository only returns values of type T and never accepts T as an input. Which declaration-site variance is appropriate to consider?
options: `out T`
`in T`
Both `in T` and `out T` on the same parameter
Variance can be selected without considering how T is used
questions.answer_key: `out T`
questions.explanation: A type parameter used only in output positions can be covariant; API design and use-site variance still need review.

questions.prompt: A file reader must be closed even when processing throws. What should a JVM Kotlin implementation normally prefer for a Closeable/AutoCloseable resource?
options: Leave it open and rely on garbage collection.
Close only on the successful path.
Wrap every failure in a broad catch and ignore it.
Use `use { ... }` so cleanup runs on exit.
questions.answer_key: Use `use { ... }` so cleanup runs on exit.
questions.explanation: The `use` pattern performs deterministic cleanup across normal and exceptional exits for compatible closeable resources.

questions.prompt: A teammate cannot reproduce a build because local Gradle and plugin versions differ. What is the best first improvement?
options: Upgrade every dependency to its newest version.
Commit a compatible Gradle Wrapper and declare/pin the project toolchain and plugin versions.
Remove the build file and compile by hand.
Hide the warning instead of checking compatibility.
questions.answer_key: Commit a compatible Gradle Wrapper and declare/pin the project toolchain and plugin versions.
questions.explanation: A wrapper and explicitly managed compatible toolchain reduce machine-to-machine variation; library/plugin compatibility still must be checked.

questions.prompt: Two coroutines update a shared mutable counter and sometimes lose increments. What is the most appropriate response?
options: Add arbitrary delays until the race seems to disappear.
Assume coroutines automatically serialize all writes.
Use an appropriate synchronization/atomic strategy or redesign to avoid shared mutable state.
Catch and ignore all exceptions.
questions.answer_key: Use an appropriate synchronization/atomic strategy or redesign to avoid shared mutable state.
questions.explanation: The race is caused by unsynchronized shared state. Select a synchronization strategy based on the operation and concurrency requirements.

questions.prompt: A unit test for a business rule makes a real network call and fails whenever the service is offline. What is the most useful test-design change?
options: Run more real network calls in every unit test.
Stub or fake the external collaborator for the unit test; test networking separately.
Skip all assertions.
Treat network errors as proof that the business rule passed.
questions.answer_key: Stub or fake the external collaborator for the unit test; test networking separately.
questions.explanation: A test double isolates the unit under test; separate integration tests verify the actual network boundary.

questions.prompt: An API key was placed in a mobile app source as a constant. What should be changed?
options: Rename it to `privateKey` and keep it in the client.
Base64-encode it and keep it in the client.
Move secret use to an authorized server-side boundary and rotate the exposed key.
Print the key only in debug mode.
questions.answer_key: Move secret use to an authorized server-side boundary and rotate the exposed key.
questions.explanation: Client-distributed apps cannot keep embedded secrets confidential; remove the exposure, rotate the key, and enforce access on the server.

questions.prompt: A Ktor endpoint accepts an item ID from a request. What is the strongest safe default before reading or changing data?
options: Trust every supplied ID if it parses as an integer.
Validate input and enforce authorization for the specific resource/action on the server.
Check authorization only in the UI.
Return raw stack traces for all failures.
questions.answer_key: Validate input and enforce authorization for the specific resource/action on the server.
questions.explanation: Parsing input is not authorization. The backend must validate the request and enforce access on the specific resource/action.

questions.prompt: A shared Kotlin Multiplatform module compiles on Android but fails for iOS because code uses a JVM-only API. What is the best architectural correction?
options: Force the JVM API into commonMain.
Disable iOS compilation permanently.
Move the JVM-specific code into a suitable platform source set and expose a common abstraction where needed.
Copy the entire application into every target.
questions.answer_key: Move the JVM-specific code into a suitable platform source set and expose a common abstraction where needed.
questions.explanation: Common source sets must use common APIs. Keep platform-specific calls in the correct target and bridge them through a deliberate abstraction.
